EPA numbers for week 4
stories.summary:
well, that was ass.



	 



	week 4's loss was an interesting one statistically because our EPA overall was exactly -3, which is what we lost by.  on the season our expected wins is 2.6, we were nearly a full win over expected (meaning we won lucky a bit) as of last week, now less than half a win over.  our luck ran out this week.



	 



	the offense was better than last week, positive EPA there at +~7.5, run was +.25, pass was just under +6, turnovers were just more negative than -5.  special teams was -1.25, which is basically whatever.  on D the run stopping was actually good, +1 EPA.  pass d was -10.  That run D includes the QB runs, if you slid those over to the passing side of the EPA (which might be fair given it was our defense against the pass that let those up) we were nearly as bad vs new england as we were vs detroit, and a lot of that was just desperation garbage time air it out stuff.  if you put stroud's runs on the pass side too, basically you are looking at quite solid run D and the worst passing d in the nfl.



	 



	we had 11 possessions, a number inflated (for both teams, both had 11) because of the last 2nd quarter shakir fumble followed by the NE turnover super quickly.  we had 5 scoring drives, the pats had 4 but made them count as they were all touch downs.



	 



	cook tore it up for basically 10 or 15 in game minutes, and was just not featured before or after that.  i bet if we had some better play calling on that last drive we don't get desperate and we come back and score for the win.



	 



	they say run to win and pass for points, but for the bills you want to pass to score and win.  the only times we have stopped anyone in the red zone has been a clock assisted fg attempt that hit by detroit, the fumble we forced on the last drive vs stroud (again, time pressure was there) and we did force some fg attempts as the chargers capsized with their horrible offense.  statistically someone might be worse, but to my eye we are the worst red zone defense in the nfl.  we are a bend and break D.  i think we had the fewest 3 and outs coming into this game, but we had some this game and some non 3 and outs were also trash.



	 



	if i'm looking for the smallest and simplest improvement that we could make as a team to change our fortunes it is as follows:



	 



	1  Red zone D.  it's so bad.  an average red zone d and we likely win every game by double digits, offensive mistakes and all.



	 



	2 penalties.  we let about 2+ drives a game extend against us due to penalties.  given how bad we are at letting sustained drives happen, that's worth like 5 points a game.  this would also have us winning our games by double digits, except the pats game which we woulda still won.



	 



	3 balance on O/situational football.  our ability for running and passing combined is pretty exceptional.  forcing the pass game situationally has hurt us bad.  the end of half drive vs detroit was bad, not going for a td on the freeby at the end of the 1st half on sunday was bad.  not having any kind of run plays going on our last drive on sunday was the worst.  cook was going strong, the pats had no real answer, but i think they knew what we were going to do based on formation and personnel and just laughed.  also, in the pass game itself the attempts to WRs is way too high.  we have done very little effectively in terms of passing to backs, and when we do well the tight ends are super involved.  every time we stray from that it gets bad.



	 



	so, the d sucks the bag vs the pass (i chose to see qb scrambles as pass d issues, not run d issues, so it's basically worst in the nfl).  dc jimmy boy needs to do something to create more havoc, even at the risk of allowing deep passing plays.  the only positive outcomes vs the pass have come from havoc.  the combo of the players we have out there and the scheme in the secondary is legit bottom of the barrel.  bad and slumping qbs are far too comfortable against us.

stories.title: USA vs. Mexico, 2026 Friendly: Man of the Match
Thoughts on the game after 2 watches
stories.summary:
I was at the game. First game at the new (awesome!!!) Stadium.



	 



	I always record and watch a 2nd time when I get home 



	 



	After watching a 2nd time I have just a few thoughts... most are fairly optimistic, just to warn you:



	 



	DL & OLBs are really good: I actually felt better about the whole D on 2nd watch, but I think we should just tip our hats to some incredible plays made by NE offensive players (especially Maye) eluding tackles that would have been made in the backfield. And I was encouraged by every single player across the front. Too bad it looks like Landon Jackson will be out now. He had an awesome game. Deonn Walker was inches away from more batted passes and tackles in the backfield or sacks. Chubb was really good... wish he could have finished a couple plays. Groot was still incredible even if he didn't get his sacks. Even Carter and Gaines were making plays. Oliver might have been the biggest disappointment.



	 



	I really want to emphasize just how awesome Groot is. Right now he's the best defensive player in football through 4 games. Keep it up! Considering how awesome Walker is also playing we look like we have 2 absolute game-wreckers who just need to stay healthy.



	 



	Hairston: Everyone has said what needs to be said. I don't know how Brady or Leonhard can justify playing him over IGB if Benford comes back healthy. And please get Benford back. I'd be perfectly fine trading Hairston if we can get anything for him. Bring Tre White back for CB3.



	 



	Defensive scheme: So much zone... why??? Maye found so many soft spots. Hairston looked completely lost in the the zone just playing flat footed. I get that Benford was out but I'd rather see Leonhard play his D. 



	 



	Keon Coleman: His best game in the NFL by far!!! Looks like a legitimate NFL WR this season. The way he played yesterday was all I think we could have hoped for. If this is the Keon we get the rest of the season and DJ Moore can get healthy, we get back to the fireworks show of week 1 & 2.



	 



	DJ Moore: Sit him. If this injury is just going to constantly be reaggravated then let's just get him healthy. He's too important. The last couple weeks Skyler Bell has reportedly been getting a lot of reps with Allen in practice. Let him roll out there with Coleman and Shakir so Moore can heal up and be back to 100% after the bye week.



	 



	Joshua Palmer: Ugh! I know he caught 2 TDs in the first 2 weeks, but he was pretty awful yesterday. He dropped a deep pass from Allen that would've been overturned but would have given the offense another play. Not remotely on the same page with Josh for multiple plays despite being in his 2nd year with him. Mainly, no fight. On the Shakir fumble he was the first on the ball, which was why Kincaid and other Bills players thought we kept the ball... but he just got outmuscled.



	 



	Alec Anderson & Dion: The left side of our OL appears to be a problem. Losing Edwards seems to be a big deal for Dawkins especially. Anderson doesn't seem terrible, but definitely a downgrade and the communication factor seems problematic.



	 



	Josh: Was anyone else getting "low-positive Josh" vibes yesterday? Maybe even stretching to last week with the weird PC where he was looking down the entire time he answered questions. Even his TD Celebrations in the 2nd half seemed subdued. Josh was still Josh a number of times and I'm not freaking out, I just hope he shakes out of whatever personal/professional funk he's in right now. Another thing... I thought his discussion of Keon insisted PC was really strange. I won't speculate, but for a game where I thought Keon actually deserved a ton of praise, Josh didn't seem to want to give it. But let's all be real here... this funk happens every year once or twice. My panic meter for Josh (and the team) is pretty close to zero right now.



	 



	Outlook: The AFC is underwhelming for a 2nd straight year. Lamar is hurt yet again. The Bengals are bungling. Sorry, but I just don't understand the conversation about the Jags being the bestteam in the AFC right now. The Broncos were clearly overrated going into the season with lot of folks calling them the AFC favorite and one of the best rosters in the NFL. Do we really believe the Raiders are good? Do we really believe the Chiefs are back? My answer to that first question is no and in part because of that answer my answer to the 2nd question is I don't think so. I do think the Chiefs will win their division now because that division just looks weaker overall and they have the easiest schedule in the NFL... so we're likely on another collision course with them in the playoffs. Let's just get through the season and finally get there! No reason to think this team can't!

stories.title: Detroit Lions at Carolina Panthers, NFL Week 4 ‘SNF’ fan discussion
A Few Thoughts about the Patriots Game, in no particular order
stories.summary:
Before anyone asks, yes I'm still pissed off and probably not objective right now.  Yes, I know the point of these is to give myself some time off so that I don't post emotionally.  And yes, I'm ignoring those rules because I think it's warranted here.  No lyrics today, because the Bills make me want to do anything but sing right now.  This feels like a playoff loss to me.  A game where we should have absolutely brought our A game against a banged up division rival.  Also, knowing our first loss in the new stadium came against the Patriots is infuriating.  And to the cheating Meathead!?



	 



	1 - McD - This was a McD coached game and it's infuriating to me.  Yes, we did try to prioritize throwing the ball downfield more than we would under McD, which is equally frustrating when you could see the Pats mimicked the Chargers gameplay to take both that and Josh scrambles away.  On offense, we were back to the WR screens (which Josh seems to really struggle not throwing low), we were throwing up 50/50 or back should fades to Coleman, and we didn't seem to know how to throw to our tight ends.  Sadly, we also didn't have the McD defense to confuse Maye, but we did bring over the defense that can't get off the field on third downs.  It was only a matter of time before our inexperienced head coaches cost us a game, and of course we pick the first division game at home against the team that beat for the division to do it.  



	 



	2 - Brady/Leonard - I did not want Brady as our Head Coach (Kubiak was my guy) and really didn't like the idea of transitioning to a 3-4 defense in the last few years of Josh's Prime, especially with Leonard openly admitting it's going to take him at least two years to get the roster needed to execute effectively.   If this doesn't work with Leonard, it will take another two years to switch back to a 4-3 or whatever scheme that coach wants.  Why did I not want Brady, because in his two years as OC, I never saw him make Josh's life easy in crucial moments.  We saw it with the two point conversions, which have been comically bad under Brady, and we are seeing Josh having to press game after game.  Where are the plays where Brady schemes guys wide open in short yardage plays?  Where's the plays to get us down the field when we only need a FG to tie, and then take some shots?  And most importantly, WHY ARE WINNING THE TOSS AND TAKING THE BALL?!  Listen, if your offense is sputtering and you need a culture shock, I get it in a one off situation, but that's not the case here.  The double dip at halftime is a huge advantage and Brady is just giving it up.  As of right now, these are the up and down arrows I have for the coaches and overall play of the Bills - On offense, the explosive plays are back, but we are way to slow to adjust when teams scheme them away.  The run game disappears for quarters at a time, and then comes back in a way that makes you wonder why we didn't go to it sooner.  On defense, we traded our inability to get pressure for a complete lack of support in our defensive backfield.  Seriously, Bishop is non-existent and the DB's are getting abused out there.  The only time we seem to get a stop is when the pressure gets home or forces an errant throw.  Have we seen a single coverage sack this year?   Right now, I'm looking for signs of things getting better and I'm struggling.  I don't feel like we have a scheme on either side of the ball and any element of surprise to start the season with a new coach and DC is gone.  Teams are clearly applying schemes to slow us down and we aren't returning the favor.  



	 



	3 - Josh - I don't know what to make of Josh right now. There were still moments where he looked like Josh, especially when he kept the play alive and found Shakir downfield for the 50 yard gain. But there were also too many little things that just looked off. He's still throwing some of those WR screens low, which completely kills the receiver's momentum. On the three and out in the second half, he put the ball on Shakir's wrong shoulder. Then there's the final interception. I'm sorry, but that's inexcusable. You're down three, you don't need a touchdown on that play, and Palmer is double covered. There was absolutely no reason to make that throw. I understand Josh is always going to believe he can make a play, and that's part of what makes him great, but those are the mistakes he has to own and get better at. You can't end a winnable game like that.  Maybe there's some truth to the rumor that Josh is nursing an injury and maybe that's why he's not running as much.  However, as we also saw with the Chargers, the Pats attacked the offensive line in a way that pushed the pocket into him and took away running lanes.  Again, another example of a team knowing how to scheme against us and us being unable to counter.  



	 



	4 - Defense - I don't even know where to start. Opening drive touchdowns allowed in both halves.  A game winning touchdown with 4 minutes left.  We were completely unprepared.  New England converted way too many 3rd and 4th downs. Maye repeatedly escaped with his legs. Receivers were running open. The pass rush couldn't finish. Hollins continued to kill us. Then when the game was ultimately put in the defense's hands, outside of one good pressure from Groot, Maye had all day before hitting the deep touchdown over IGB and then they converted the two-point conversion with almost no resistance. There were individual moments. Landon Jackson helped create the fumble. Alford got the interception before halftime, albeit with a very fortunate bounce. Walker finally made a big play with the tackle for loss. Groot disrupted some plays. They even started getting some third down stops later in the game. But there was never a stretch where I felt like this defense was dictating anything. That's probably what bothers me most. New England didn't have to overcome this defense. For most of the game, Buffalo was reacting to whatever Maye and the Patriots wanted to do. When we finally needed one stop to give Josh a chance to win the game, they went right down the field and scored. That's simply not good enough, especially against a team missing their top players on both sides of the ball. 



	 



	5 - Death by Stupidity - Can someone explain to me how McGovern can be called Offside? I'm genuinely asking because I don't know what the refs saw there. Beyond that, I feel like every week I'm writing about some completely avoidable mistake that either kills a Bills drive or gives the other team life. Dawkins had multiple penalties. Bass screws up a kickoff and gives New England the ball around the 40. Shakir fumbles while we're already in field goal range before halftime. We pin New England deep and immediately give them 15 yards on a personal foul. Hairston gets called for defensive holding on 3rd and goal and gives them a fresh set of downs. We even had some pretty obvious holds on Maye scrambles that weren't called. I'm not going to blame the refs for the loss because the Bills did more than enough stupid things on their own, but they certainly didn't help. Good teams are going to beat you enough on their own. You can't keep helping them.



	 



	6 - Palmer - I'm officially concerned and I think it's time for Palmer to start dropping down the depth chart. There have now been multiple deep balls where he looks like he either doesn't know where the ball is or can't adjust to it once it's in the air. We saw it against Houston and it happened again multiple times today. That's a pretty big problem for someone who is supposed to be one of our downfield threats. At some point, I'd rather give those snaps to someone else and see what they can do. The final interception isn't on Palmer because Josh never should have thrown that ball into double coverage, but there's clearly something missing between these two right now. Palmer has had enough opportunities and I'm not seeing anything that justifies keeping him ahead of other guys on the depth chart.  At this point, if Palmer is only going to be available downfield and shaky at best, let's see Bell get his opportunities.



	 



	7 - Maye - I'm sure we're going to hear all week about how great Drake Maye looked, and he did play well, but I'm more interested in why the Bills defense made him look like an MVP again. For eight straight games, other defenses figured out ways to make things difficult for him and then Buffalo comes along and lets him look completely comfortable. There was seemingly no attempt to contain him as a runner. He repeatedly escaped the pocket and picked up yards with his legs, and when he stayed in the pocket, he usually had all day to throw. Guys were running open all over the field and Hollins killed us again. That's what makes this so frustrating. It's not like nobody knows how to slow Maye down. We just watched eight straight defenses do it and then Buffalo couldn't replicate any of it. Outside of a few disruptive plays from Groot and the pressure that helped create the early fumble, Maye looked way too comfortable. That's how bad this defensive performance was.



	 



	8 - Offensive Line - This might have been the worst I've seen this offensive line look in a while. Dawkins got beat almost immediately for a sack and then compounded it with multiple penalties. Even after the defense created the Maye fumble and handed the offense an opportunity, a Dawkins hold helped wipe out the Palmer deep ball and Buffalo ended up punting. We weren't getting the normal push in the running game either, which took away one of the biggest strengths of this offense. I still believe this is a very good offensive line, but we've seen this before. When things start going wrong up front, they seem to snowball. Against a defense that was already making things difficult, the penalties and protection issues made it that much harder for Josh and the offense to ever find a rhythm.



	 



	9 - Defensive Line - It was only a matter of time before the sack streak ended, but Groot was still an absolute force out there.  It looks like the Pats did a good job of moving the pocket around just enough for the Bills front line to just miss him. Even with that, at some point, "almost" has to turn into sacks. We just watched Maye escape pressure and extend plays all game. Groot is supposed to be one of the guys capable of ending those plays before they start. Disrupting plays is valuable, but against a quarterback who was killing us with both his arm and legs, we needed somebody to actually get him on the ground.  It looks like Dorian was meant to spy at times, and was very ineffective at it.  And while I never want to blame a player for getting injured, Oliver's lack of ability to stay in games is a real issue.  He simply isn't reliable.  Sadly, his cap his isn't going to allow us to move on from him.  



	 



	10 - Hairston - That was a brutal game for Hairston. I know he's young and there are going to be growing pains, but New England went after him in some of the biggest moments and he didn't respond. On 4th down, Maye completed one right in front of him for the conversion. Then on 3rd and goal, Hairston gets called for defensive holding and gives the Patriots a fresh set of downs. Two plays later, he's the one giving up the touchdown. That's basically an entire scoring drive where his mistakes directly helped keep New England on the field.



	What made it worse was that there were plays where he just looked confused. This wasn't simply a young corner getting beat by a great receiver. There were moments where it didn't look like he knew where he was supposed to be. I'm all for allowing young players to develop and play through mistakes, but there's a difference between getting beat and repeatedly hurting the defense in critical situations. This was easily one of the worst games I've seen from Hairston and teams are going to keep attacking him until he proves they shouldn't.  I mean, Doubs looked like an all-pro out there after being a laughing stock all season.  



	 



	***My apologies to Keon Coleman who is really stepping up when we need him most.  I'd love to sing his praises, but this loss doesn't deserve praise.



	 



	 



	Emotional Playoff Pain - Okay, here's your real overreaction, so please feel free to stop reading now.  I have zero faith in this teams ability to make a meaningful run this season.  Looking at our wins so far, only the Lions game is mildly respectable.  Our offense is trending down.  Our defense looks lost and is getting injured.  Homefield advantage doesn't seem to be helping us at all.  Seriously, has any team look rattled in our new home?  Josh is still Josh in that he'll win you a bunch of plays, but can still press and lose the game for us (Yes, I know that not one player can lose you a game).  We went from the potential of being 4-0 with a stranglehold on the division to a really strong chance of being 2nd place in the division next week.  I believe in any given Sunday, but also believe we are going to get taken to the woodshed next week against the Rams.  The Raiders don't look like an easy game either anymore.  Then we get the Ravens at home.  Unless this defense magically figures out how to make a stop, we are going to need to score 30 every week for a change to win, and the offense isn't looking like they are going to be able to keep that going.  Teams can apparently scheme Kincaid away and our saving grace aged WR who never gets hurt can't finish a game.  So yeah, give me something to sing about.  Two of our wins came against winless teams and we just revived the Patriots season.  I'm pissed and I think I deserve to be pissed.  After 10k per PSL and sell job on these new coaches in the final years of Josh's prime, it's really hard to believe Josh isn't going to end up being Marino 2.0.



	 



	 



	*I know I'm late to the party, but WGR is abysmal.  The entire post game show was 40 minutes of them talking about what could have happened if the Bills won.  There was no game analysis, no play breakdowns, nothing beyond replaying the Josh interception.  I need to find something else to listen to live postgame.

stories.title: Sabres rally for late win against shorthanded Blackhawks
stories.summary:
Score: Buffalo Sabres 4, Chicago Blackhawks 3



Shots: Buffalo 28, Chicago 15



Buffalo Sabres Goals: Quinn (Metsa); Thompson (Crevier, Norris); Dahlin (Krebs, Samuelsson); Kulich (Power, Thompson)



Chicago Blackhawks Goals: Donato (Vlasic, Lardis); Bertuzzi (Teravainen, Vlasic); Moore (Frondell, Vlasic)



The Buffalo Sabres sneak past the Chicago Blackhawks, who were down number one defenseman Bowen Byram and top player Connor Bedard, 4-3 in their first win of the season.



First Period River Hockey



Though they were pressured on the first shift, thanks in part to an amped-up Jordan Greenway, the Sabres dictated the pace for the first five minutes of the first. They had their legs ready early, and while they couldn’t cash in for an early lead, it led to a handful of scoring chances. 



That early work would be for naught, though, as Ryan Donato would bury a chance past Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen at the 8:00 minute mark of the period to give the Blackhawks an early lead. Blackhawks defenseman Alex Vlasic carried the puck low, and while four Sabres were in the area of the crease, Vlasic was able to find the open space to set up for Donato, who made no mistake. 



This goal did not discourage the Sabres, rather it seemed to invigorate them. The Benson-Ostlund-Quinn trio combined for a couple of high-quality chances, while the line of Ryan McLeod, Konsta Helenius, and Peyton Krebs generated a quick strike chance. This, once again, was all for naught. 



At the 11:49 mark, just after their scoring chance they couldn’t capitalize on, that line, particularly Helenius and Krebs, helped contribute to yet another defensive blunder, as Tyler Bertuzzi was left all alone in the crease, able to bury the easiest tap-in a player can have, thanks to a feed from Teuvo Teravaianen. 



Despite the 2-0 hole they dug themselves, the Sabres kept pushing but couldn’t beat Blackhawks goalie Spencer Knight. Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin was robbed once on a cross-ice feed from Quinn, then again on a chance in the high-slot a few seconds later, when the Blackhawks also benefited from an early whistle, as officials ruled Knight had the puck covered when he almost certainly did not. 



Finally, though, persistence paid off, as Quinn got the Sabres on the board on their 13th shot of the period. Quinn found space, carried the puck to the high slot, and using Blackhawks defenseman Kevin Korchinski as a screen, sniped the corner to cut the deficit to 2-1. While Zach Metsa got the lone assist, the goal wouldn’t have happened without a nice pinch by Louis Crevier, who used his reach to keep the play alive. 



While the score went into the first intermission at 2-1, the crowd did get one last thing to cheer about before the horn sounded, as Patrick Kane, who was met with a cacophony of boos the whole game, got lit up by Mattias Samuelsson in the dying seconds of the third. 



Knight was the story of the first for the Blackhawks, who had two xGoals of chances put on him and was able to allow only one. It was overall a very “River Hockey” type period with high paced play and defensive lapses. 



A full 60 (pages)



The Sabres came out firing in the second, generating a few shots in the first few minutes, and missing on a few others, with McLeod unable to center a pass to the slot and Quinn overskating a puck. Knight also made a nice glove save on Sam Carrick from the slot, then another on Quinn a couple minutes later. 



The Sabres kept the pressure on and were rewarded with the equalizer just six minutes into the second. Thompson won a faceoff back to Crevier, who ripped a shot from the point that deflected off Thompson’s stick for his first of the season. 



The Sabres were not satisfied with a tie, as the pressure continued relentlessly after the game was tied up. Knight had to keep his head in the game, quite literally, as he used his mask to deny Olen Zellweger of a potential go ahead goal. 



The game hit a lull in the middle part of the second, as both teams defaulted to feeling each other out. The Blackhawks would get the game’s first power play almost 12 minutes into the frame, as Josh Doan committed a hooking penalty. The Sabres had a huge question mark over the head of their penalty kill after their first game, but they answered the bell on their first opportunity of the game, though Luukkonen did have to make a really nice save in tight as the Blackhawks power play expired. 



A flurry of chances, highlighted by Helenius being denied on a shot in tight off a behind the net feed by McLeod, still couldn’t give the Sabres the lead, though the constant pressure did give them their first power play of the game. 



As has been the case for the past two seasons, the power play killed the momentum for the Sabres, as Thompson single handedly killed zone pressure on three separate occasions, one of which led to a breakaway that Luukkonen had to stop. The second unit got a nice look, but as the power play expired, the Blackhawks found themselves on a two-on-one rush with McLeod as the only Sabre back. Oliver Moore, who came out of the penalty box, made no mistake, as Luukkonen was unable to get enough to keep the puck out of the net, giving the Blackhawks the lead back, 3-2. 



It’s a save the Sabres’ goalie could have made, but it was yet another opportunistic play by the Blackhawks, who preferred quality over quantity in this game, particularly in the period, where they only mustered four shots on goal. 



Lock In and Lock Down



The third period started with an early Sabres power play, as local villain Kane found himself in the box, but as it stands there is no more efficient way to protect a lead than to give the Sabres a power play. 



The Sabres then spent most of the third period attempting to carry the puck into the Blackhawks’ zone, only for them to get met at the blue line and have to chase the puck back. However, the breakthrough finally happened, off the stick of the captain, Rasmus Dahlin, thanks to a nice feed from Peyton Krebs on a counter-rush. Dahlin took the pass in the high slot and sniped it home to tie it up for the Sabres again. 



The Sabres would have another great chance a few minutes later as Quinn found himself all alone in front of the net after Benson broke up a play at center ice to set him up. Quinn however slid the puck wide, unable to give the Sabres their first lead of the game. 



While it looked like the Sabres would get a late chance on the power play, as Cole Smith found himself in the box for tripping, Benson would answer with a tripping penalty of his own to put it at a four on four. Thankfully, this is advantageous for the Sabres.



At the end of a shift, Thompson and Kulich found themselves on a two-on-one, and while Kulich couldn’t bury the shot, he would get another chance. The puck found Owen Power, who found Kulich yet again, who made no mistake on his second opportunity, giving the Sabres the lead, 4-3, with his first of the season, with just 6:40 left on the clock. 



After taking the lead, the team locked in defensively, allowing the Blackhawks just one shot on goal after taking the lead. 



Wrap Up



All in all, it was a bit of a sloppy game from the Sabres, but they were able to rally against an opponent that was missing their best forward and defenseman. But, they don’t ask how, they ask how many, and a number in the left column is exactly what the Sabres needed.



Other notes



There were a few interesting lineup changes near the end of the game. Metsa played just one shift in the third period, and McLeod was flipped to the fourth line with Carrick and Beck Malenstyn. The group of them did not see the ice after taking the lead. Kulich was bumped up to play with Krebs and Helenius, who contributed to what would be the game winning goal. 



On Kulich, he was clearly very emotional in his post game interview. It had to be a nice moment for him, from thinking he may never play hockey again to scoring a game winner. It should be the first of many he scores over the rest of his NHL career. 



Bowen Byram will have to wait for his Buffalo homecoming moment, as he missed the game tending to a family matter.

stories.title: Game #2 Preview & Open Thread: Sabres vs Blackhawks
stories.summary:
Byram Will Not Play in Buffalo Return



Unfortunately, there is only one “revenge game” tonight. Former defenseman Bowen Byram will not play for Chicago tonight. Blackhawks coach Jeff Blashill said Byram is tending to a family matter. That means Sabres fans will have to wait for Byram’s first game back at KeyBank Center since Buffalo traded him to Chicago this summer. Jordan Greenway is still expected to be in Chicago’s lineup and will face the Sabres for the first time since the trade. Byram’s absence forces Chicago to reshuffle its defense. Kevin Korchinski and Ethan Del Mastro will both make their season debuts after sitting out the Blackhawks’ first two games. Byram didn’t have the best first game, but I’m sure it will improve. Byram got everything he wanted when he was traded: to be the #1 D-man and a big contract, so “revenge” is a little harsh.



Zellweger Is In



There is no longer much uncertainty surrounding Olen Zellweger, and the Byram replacement will get his first look in the blue and gold. Zellweger will make his Sabres season debut tonight after recovering from the concussion he suffered during the preseason against Columbus. He practiced alongside Owen Power on Friday and is listed with Power on Buffalo’s second defense pair in the NHL’s latest projected lineup. That gives Buffalo another high-end skating and puck-moving option on the back end and changes the look of the defense from Thursday’s loss in Columbus. The NHL’s current projection has Matt Grzelcyk returning to the lineup alongside Louis Crevier; they played together in Chicago last year on the third pair, with Zach “fighting” Metsa listed as a scratch.

Final Thoughts



The Byram storyline has changed, but plenty remains around Buffalo’s home opener. Jordan Greenway returns to KeyBank Center in a Blackhawks sweater, Patrick Kane is back in Buffalo, and Olen Zellweger will make his Sabres debut. 



Chicago is also changing two-thirds of its bottom four on defense after surrendering 11 goals through its first two games. For Buffalo, the task remains the same: take advantage of a struggling team, clean up special teams, and establish control early rather than letting Chicago hang around. Last season’s Atlantic Division banner goes up in the rafters tonight.



Then Buffalo gets back to work.

Buffalo Sabres Goals: Samuelsson 1st (Ostlund, Power) Quinn 1st (Benson, Ostlund)  Helenius 1st (McLeod, Power)Columbus Blue Jackets Goals: Sillinger 1st (Coyle, Mateychuk) Knies 1st (Coyle, Werenski) Fantilli 1st (Werenski, Knies) Knies 2nd (Andrae, Johnson) Monahan 1st ( Nichushkin, Voronkov) Olivier 1st (Coyle)



“Frustrated Incorporated”



Minus 1: Sammy! Then WHAMMY!



Buffalo got a good chance just seconds into the game when Tage Thompson rang one off the iron. Josh Doan followed that up with a nice pass from Josh Norris, taking the puck right to the net, but Jet Greaves of Columbus made a quality save. The Blue Jackets then put on a strong forecheck but couldn’t get the puck to the net for a shot. Carson Soucy was called for cross-checking Sabres forward Jack Quinn, giving Buffalo’s much-maligned power play its first opportunity of the season.



It didn’t last long.



After fumbling the puck at least twice, TNT was called for hooking, negating the rest of the man advantage. That opened the ice for 4-on-4 play and gave Mattias Samuelsson plenty of room to let one rip. Sammy cashed in with a wicked shot that eluded Greaves. Noah Ostlund and Owen Power picked up the assists on Buffalo’s first goal of the new season.



Ten minutes in, the shots were just 3-2 in favor of the Sabres.



Buffalo picked up its fourth and fifth shots while enjoying some quality zone time, but a Columbus breakout would tie the game. Charlie Coyle tried to split the Sabres defense, which closed in on him, but Coyle made a great play to drop the puck back to an open Cole Sillinger. He fired a snapper past a surprised Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen. The Sabres’ forwards were caught too deep and couldn’t get back to cover the man in the slot.



A little later, Buffalo fumbled the puck in front of its own net with some inopportune passing. Samuelsson had to tie up his man to recover, bringing him down and taking a penalty in the process. Columbus cashed in quickly as Matthew Knies snapped a shot on UPL from about 15 feet out that found the twine. The Jackets had now collected four straight shots and two goals. They added another on their next shot. Adam Fantilli’s long-distance blast had eyes, beating Luukkonen again.



The Sabres’ first-period collapse was painful to watch and incredibly discouraging after scoring first on the road. Buffalo’s new and undermanned defense was certainly not in midseason form, and neither was UPL. The Sabres weren’t aggressive enough defensively, repeatedly backing in instead of challenging the Columbus attack. This was a serious shake-your-head period—one Buffalo desperately needed to put behind it. Would they?



Plus 1: Two on the Board but One Against



A quick turnover to start the period allowed Jack Quinn to bring the game back within one. Buffalo held the puck in at the blue line, where Zach Benson came up with it and quickly dished it to Quinn. Benson then drove to the net, taking a Columbus defender with him. Quinn cut wide, setting himself up for the shot before zipping the puck past Jet Greaves. It was a huge goal to start the middle frame and exactly what the Blue and Gold needed.



Buffalo found some new life after the goal, generating more zone time and pressure. The Sabres would draw a penalty on a strong forecheck as Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen headed to the bench. The whistle eventually blew with the puck rolling in front of Buffalo’s empty net. Mathieu Olivier decided he would break the unwritten rules and fired the puck into the yawning cage, and Sabres defenseman Zach Metsa let him know that wasn’t going to fly, giving him a good shove. The hulking Blue Jackets enforcer then decided to go ham, attacking Metsa and firing away with wild punches. Metsa was clearly overmatched and undersized, but to his credit, Zach hung in there. He absorbed Olivier’s relentless barrage and even managed to sneak in a few shots of his own. Metsa did his best to shield himself from the assault, but where were the refs on that one? A much smaller player was essentially in survival mode against a significantly bigger opponent, and the zebras simply stood back and watched. Way to go, NHL.



Buffalo would receive a five-on-three advantage following the incident, but the Sabres couldn’t cash in. A two-man advantage was the perfect opportunity to tie the game, and good teams find a way to capitalize in those situations. Buffalo didn’t, and it would come back to bite them as Columbus reestablished its two-goal lead. Matthew Knies scored again, giving him three points on the night. The former Toronto Maple Leaf seemed possessed, apparently determined to continue finding success against Buffalo even after leaving the Atlantic Division.



The Sabres would get their fourth power play of the night shortly afterward, but once again failed to score. However, Buffalo continued to keep the pressure on and finally found twine moments after the penalty expired. Konsta Helenius scored his first goal of the season after receiving a beautiful cross-ice pass from Ryan McLeod. Owen Power picked up his second assist of the game on the play as well.



The Sabres generated some good zone time for the remainder of the period, but couldn’t find the equalizer. After 40 minutes, Columbus still held a 4-3 lead.







Minus 2: Sammy’s Double Whammy



Buffalo continued to get some zone time early in the period, generating a few chances while pressing the attack. Benson and Ostlund were standouts among the forward ranks. Luukkonen then came up with his best save of the game, getting a piece of the puck while sliding across the crease to deny a Columbus 2-on-1. He had faced just 16 shots to that point, but four of them had already found the back of the net. He remained focused though.



Owen Power then had his stick slashed in half as Sillenger was sent off the ice. Another chance for the dreaded Buffalo power play. Once again, failure, though the Sabres came close with a shot off the post with 3 seconds left. Columbus was all over the puck carrier and was winning most of the face offs. UPL then came up big again, denying Knies of a hat trick on a breakaway. It wasn’t his best outing for sure but he kept his team in it for much of the third period.



Samuelsson then took his second penalty of the evening, this time for tripping. The Sabres nearly killed it off, but Sean Monahan tipped the puck past UPL with just two seconds remaining on the man advantage. Just like that, Columbus had a 5-3 lead. Both of Sammy’s penalties ultimately resulted in Blue Jackets power-play goals.



Buffalo eventually pulled UPL, and, well, we all know how that usually goes. You have a better chance of hitting the Lotto than the Sabres cashing in on a 6-on-5 advantage. After several more puck fumbles, Mathieu Olivier found the empty net to seal a 6-3 Columbus victory. As discussed before the game, the Sabres simply do not match up well against Columbus, for whatever reason. It was a disappointing way to start the new year, with mental mistakes and poor puck control plaguing Buffalo throughout the night. The defense also failed to attack the way it needed to, allowing the Blue Jackets far too much room to operate.



Overall, it was a frustrating game to watch. The Sabres have plenty of work to do and will need to clean up several problem areas before they take the ice again. What a ginormous disappointment. We waited all summer for THAT???



Final Thoughts:



Once again, special teams were a major issue in this game. The power play went 0-for-5, while the penalty kill managed to go just 1-for-3. There’s your game right there. Those are simply dreadful numbers, and the struggles on the faceoff dot only made matters worse. Draws have been an issue with this group for some time, and tonight was no different. Buffalo won just 41 percent of tonight’s faceoffs, including losing many while on the man advantage.



Rasmus Dahlin and Tage Thompson were very quiet in this game, not a good winning recipe.



The Sabres now turn their attention to the Chicago Blackhawks for their home opener on Saturday, October 3rd, at 7 p.m. at KeyBank Center. Former Buffalo defenseman Bo Byram will make his first return to the building.

“With a rebel yell, more, more, more. More, more, more!”



With the playoff drought monkey finally off the Sabres’ backs, you would have thought that the Sabrehood would be somewhat sated. Instead, one would say expectations are absolutely sky-high going into tonight’s game. The fans are ready for a Cup-run and last season’s eventual elimination was just a blip in that timeline. 



The Sabres are going to be hard-pressed to repeat that ridiculous late-season run – they went 29-9-5 from when the calendar turned to 2026, the best record in the league with only Stanley Cup champions Carolina Hurricanes one point behind them and everyone else chasing their dust.   



2. Maintain The Level



Buffalo has gotten to their division-winning berth last season by playing high intensity hockey, and they will have to quickly find those levels this season too. The Sabres didn’t make any marquee additions over the offseason, and lost core players Alex Tuch and Bowen Byram. It looks like Olen Zellweger is being touted as the Byram replacement, but otherwise the expectation is that youngsters on the team are going to all make a respective step up.  



Even more importantly, can the three-headed goalie monster replicate their incredible form from last season? Their .899 combined save percentage was second in the league and carried them to the playoffs.



3. A Pesky Opponent



Columbus have been a bit of a bogey team for the Sabres for some time now, their hard-hitting physical game has frustrated the Sabres often enough over the last few seasons with Buffalo 6-7-2 in the last five years. The Blue Jackets traded away Kirill Marchenko and Elvis Merzlikins and added Matthew Knies, and will have to decide who they really are as they seek a new identity. 



Led by star defenseman Zach Werenski and young center Adam Fantilli and boosted by veterans Charlie Coyle, Sean Monahan and Valeri Nichushkin with another young playmaker in Kent Johnson, there’s still lots of talent in this side. stories.title: Buffalo Sabres sign defenseman Louis Crevier to four-year extension
stories.summary:
Even before he has played his first game for the Buffalo Sabres tonight, Louis Crevier has decided he wants to stick around, signing a four-year contract extension worth $16 million ($4M AAV). 



The 6’8″ defenseman had signed a two-year, $1.8 million contract with the Chicago Blackhawks on July 17, 2025, before being traded to the Buffalo Sabres in June 2026, and this extension marks a big raise for the hulking player. The Sabres now have five defensemen signed through the end of the 2028-29 season, which is a sign of stability at the position. 




The Buffalo Sabres have signed defenseman Louis Crevier to a four-year extension with an AAV of $4 million. pic.twitter.com/n57zNRKcu3— Buffalo Sabres PR (@SabresPR) October 1, 2026




Crevier joined the Sabres as part of the return for star defenseman Bowen Byram who went to the Windy City. The 25-year-old dman has featured in 134 career NHL games after getting drafted 188th overall by the Blackhawks in the 2020 NHL Draft. He has scored 10 goals with 22 assists, and was ranked second in Chicago last season in a couple of key defensive metrics with 95 blocked shots and 124 hits.



Lindy Ruff is happy with what he has seen so far in practice and in the preseason games – 



“When I’ve watched him at practice, we’ve had lots of discussions about him. We’ve watched him in the games, he’s moved the puck well and skated well. There was a little concern coming off [shoulder] surgery this summer, but everything looks great. I think this will be a great fit for our hockey club.”



Crevier for his part just wanted to settle his future before the season started – 



“I’m really happy. It’s something I’ve worked at for awhile now, and I’m just super glad it’s behind me. Just having stability, I think will help me a ton to play hockey. 



“Everyone was really welcoming, and since it happened in the summer, I was free to process more-and-more information, learn names and stuff, even before I came into Buffalo. I think that helped a lot. It was just super easy, honestly.”



About his fellow blue-liners, the dman was very complimentary – 



“I think they’re all really good players, so it helps a lot. In Chicago, it was the same even earlier in the year last year. We were playing seven defensemen, so I feel like I’m used to playing with different guys.”



Crevier has been the most successful seventh rounder so far from that 2020 draft with 134 games played, with Ilya Solovyov of the Pittsburgh Penguins behind him at 45 games and a guy who featured in the Rochester local news shoveling his sidewalk (Devon Levi) in third with 39 games played.

stories.summary:
The Sabres are coming off an impressive but costly win over Columbus on Tuesday night at KeyBank Center. The team lost two defensemen in Mattias Samuelsson and newcomer Olen Zellweger.



Samuelsson suffered a lower-body injury, likely while blocking a shot, and his prognosis is week-to-week. That’s certainly not what you want to see with the official first puck drop of the season right around the corner. Rasmus Dahlin’s defensive partner will now be out for at least a handful of games, maybe more.



To add insult to yet another injury, Zellweger will miss at least a week, and potentially longer, with a concussion. Olen was having himself a nice preseason game until he was leveled by a “regular-season” type of hit in the second period while setting up a teammate.



Well wishes to both players. Hopefully, Mattias and Olen will be back in the lineup sooner rather than later. Buffalo’s defensive depth looks like it will be tested early to start the season now. Let’s just hope the team can skate away from the final two preseason tilts without any further damage.



The Sabres will ice a much less potent lineup tonight against Detroit, with most of their expected roster players sitting this one out. Konsta Helenius and Noah Ostlund will be in the lineup for Buffalo, though, along with Jiri Kulich again. So at least fans will get to see some of our young guns in action tonight.
